H1 is now adequately supported and H5 — the only competing hypothesis naming a different origin (our egress/DNS vs. the partner) — has been actively weakened rather than merely dismissed.

Grounding: every hop of H1's chain rests on VERIFIED findings. External node with has_telemetry:false and zero change records [F13,F15] -> uniform outbound failure to that single host across BOTH operations, 163+146 5000ms connect timeouts plus 161 partner-issued 503s carrying x-partner-request-id [F19,F23] -> exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate moves identically to error_rate, latency steps 128ms->5000-5600ms with no CPU/request_rate anomaly [F10,F12,F22] -> breaker OPEN 11:03:26 [F11] -> order-service 504 'exchange-gateway call failed (placeOrder)' with p99 pinned at the 5s timeout [F8,F9] -> second independent caller (market-data-service) starved from the same 11:00-11:02 onset with no error of its own and flat p99 ~40ms [F25,F26,F27] -> no recovery after the 11:16Z rollback: upstream_error_rate 45.86% and upstream_latency ~9.3s through 12:55Z [F28,F29].

The failing hop precedes the reported service's first error, so no internal change at 10:48Z can be the cause. H2/H3/H4 each contradict multiple verified findings (post-rollback persistence F28-F30; outbound-only signature F10/F11/F23; wrong branch and ~100min gap F18).

Scope: both callers of the shared hop are affected and neither caller's own code path is; exchange-gateway has no other internal downstream (F16), so the hypothesis explains every affected service, including market-data-service which the suspected change never touched.

Alternatives: H5's requirement — a partial/lossy local path that still lets 161 partner responses through — survives only as an untestable residual, and the measurable evidence runs against it: no DNS/name-resolution/'connection refused'/'no route to host' line exists in the complete log pattern set (F20), the node's own metrics are flat (F22), and the failure is uniform across the only destination and both operations (F19). The round-2 task set asked exactly the discriminating questions and none produced evidence favoring H5. H5's causal chain still has an unevidenced first hop, correctly flagged by the automated check.

Data quality: the node exposes no DNS/egress/packet-loss/retransmit metric at all [F21] — a permanent data-source limitation, not an unanswered question, so it is a reason to cap confidence and record an assumption, not to keep querying. exchange-api has no telemetry by design [F5,F15], so a partner status page or out-of-band connect test is not obtainable through the team's tools. The truncated log listing (471 matched / 40 returned) does not affect the complete top_patterns aggregate that F19/F20 rest on.

Calibration: the residual uncertainty is confined to one secondary detail — partner-internal fault vs. a degraded path between us and the partner that still permits partner answers. Both readings are external to the fleet and imply the same immediate action (escalate/failover the exchange route, do not further chase the order-service rollback).
